title: Myth: a raise can make you take home less

lines.text: Myth: a raise can bump you into a higher tax bracket and leave you with less money.

scene.myth: A raise can push you into a higher tax bracket and shrink your pay.
scene.fact: Only the dollars [above the line] get the higher rate.

lines.text: Fact: federal income tax brackets don't work that way. Only the dollars above each line get the higher rate.

scene.myth: A raise can push you into a higher tax bracket and shrink your pay.
scene.fact: Only the dollars [above the line] get the higher rate.

lines.text: Simple example. Say the 22% bracket starts at fifty thousand, and you get a raise from forty-nine to fifty-one thousand.
lines.say: Simple example. Say the twenty-two percent bracket starts at fifty thousand, and you get a raise from forty-nine to fifty-one thousand.

lines.text: The first thousand of your raise is taxed at 12%. Only the thousand above the line is taxed at 22%.
lines.say: The first thousand of your raise is taxed at twelve percent. Only the thousand above the line is taxed at twenty-two percent.

lines.text: That's three hundred forty dollars in federal income tax. You keep the rest of the two thousand dollar raise.
So take the raise. Higher brackets only touch the top slice.

scene.headline: Take the [raise]
scene.sub: Brackets only tax the top slice

lines.text: That's the money. See you at the next bell.
